newsitem.title: USA: Leon County, Fla., revises sales tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Leon County, Fla., revises sales tax plan.

text.p: Florida's Leon County Commission has revised a proposed sales tax extension to fund lake restoration projects, the Tallahassee Democrat reported Tuesday.

The one-cent local option sales tax is scheduled to end in 2004. The revised proposal would extend it for one year, raising $15 million for lake cleanup projects. Commissioners said that if voters approve the plan in a February referendum they will roll back property taxes that would otherwise be used for lake cleanup.
The county commission originally proposed a two-year sales tax extension, and wanted to use the added revenue for road projects, a new jail and lake cleanup.
The Tallahassee City Commission opposed the plan because all of the targeted projects were outside the city limits and because the list of projects was not specific enough.

The Tallahassee City Commission has not yet voted on the revised plan. Leon County can put the proposal on the ballot without city approval, but the two would have to agree on how the money could be spent if the referendum passed.
